question: Should OpenClaw adopt the proposed installation-wide two-file GRDB storage model for Apple clients, including its cache-reset and durable-state migration contract, before the Android follow-up exists?
rationale: This is a durable client-state architecture change with cross-platform follow-on implications; tests can validate implementation details but cannot choose the long-lived storage ownership contract.

options.title: Approve the Apple storage contract
options.body: Accept the two-database ownership model after maintainers verify upgrade and recovery evidence for both iOS and macOS.

options.title: Require a narrower compatibility plan
options.body: Keep existing durable storage ownership until the migration and cross-platform contract are reduced or documented more explicitly.

options.title: Pause for cross-platform design alignment
options.body: Defer landing until the Android ownership model and shared invariants are agreed as one product direction.

recommendation.title: Approve the Apple storage contract
recommendation.body: Accept the two-database ownership model after maintainers verify upgrade and recovery evidence for both iOS and macOS.

likelyOwner.reason: The linked design issue and implementation are both owned by this contributor, who is also assigned to the PR.
